newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Extra costs drag on Philips consumer earnings.
newsitem.headline: Extra costs drag on Philips consumer earnings.

text.p: Philips said on Thursday launch costs for new products and a big advertising campaign to promote the Philips brand name in the U.S. had weighed on its second-quarter 1997 earnings.
Profits from consumer products dipped to 62 million guilders ($30.2 million) in the second quarter from 206 million in the first.

Chief financial officer Jan Hammen told Reuters Financial TV that Philips had spent "several tens of millions of dollars" on familiarising U.S. consumers with the Philips name, linking it to the better-known Magnavox brand which Philips also owns.
The U.S. advertising campaign is part of new chairman Cor Boonstra's drive to revitalise the Philips name into a powerful global brand.
Hammen said second-quarter earnings were also held back by upfront costs for a new, lightweight mobile GSM phone, the Genie, due to go on sale later this year.
"Once we begin to ship the Genie it will have a dramatic impact on our earnings," he said.
Philips vice-chairman Dudley Eustace said new consumer products such as digital video discs (DVD) and recordable compact discs would in time contribute to Philips' earnings.
But it took a long time for new products to gain consumer acceptance and become profitable, he said, recalling that it took 10 years for compact discs to become a mass-market product.
"These are products which will take over in due course but they will not take over overnight," he said.
Eustace said that when new products were launched, they actually depressed profits, and it was only when volumes rose and price-cost ratios improved that they became profitable.

Eustace said Philips had delayed plans for the European launch of its Web TV product -- a TV set which allows consumers to browse through the Internet -- because it had got off to a slower than expected start in the United States.
